findings.title: Update re-POSTs secrets that already exist
findings.body:
On every update, `insertSecrets` POSTs all of `props.secrets` to the bulk create endpoint, including secrets that already exist in the store.

Re-running a stack with unchanged secrets (or changing only a value) will likely be rejected by Cloudflare as a duplicate. The update then fails. The test avoids this only because it renames every secret.

Fix: diff against `listSecrets`. Create only the new names and PATCH the existing secrets by id to change their values.

findings.title: Secrets Store binding is wired to a secret named after the binding, not the store
findings.body:
Cloudflare's `secrets_store` binding points at a single secret (`store_id` plus `secret_name`). At runtime, `env.X.get()` takes no argument and returns that one secret.

Here `secret_name` is set to `bindingName`. With `bindings: { SECRETS: store }`, the worker binds to a secret literally called `SECRETS`, which normally does not exist. Deploy or access then fails.

The documented usage `env.SECRETS.get("API_KEY")`, and the `SecretsStoreBinding.get(secretName)` type in bound.ts, do not match the platform's model.

Fix: bind per secret. Emit one `secrets_store` binding for each secret in the store, or require the user to bind a specific secret. Update the Bound type to `get(): Promise<string>`.

findings.title: Secrets Store bindings silently dropped from wrangler.json
findings.body:
The comment says these bindings are handled through a `secrets_store_secrets` array. Nothing ever adds to such an array, so the binding is omitted from the generated wrangler.json.

As a result, local dev and wrangler-based tooling will not see the binding.

Fix: collect the bindings into `spec.secrets_store_secrets` as `{ binding, store_id, secret_name }`.

findings.title: Unrelated change drops describe-block name from test scope ids
findings.body:
This rewrite of the shared test harness removes the `describe` suite name prefix from each test's scope name. The Secrets Store request does not cover it.

Tests with the same name in different `describe` blocks of one file now share a scope. Their resources and state collide, and one test's destroy can delete another's resources.

Revert this hunk.

findings.title: Secrets are created with empty scopes, so Workers cannot use them
findings.body:
Secrets Store secrets must be scoped (for example `["workers"]`) before a Worker binding can read them.

Creating them with `scopes: []` means any Worker bound to these secrets cannot access them.

Fix: default the scopes to `["workers"]`, or make them configurable.

findings.title: Tautological assertion compares the id to itself
findings.body:
`expect(secretsStore.id).toEqual(secretsStore.id)` always passes, so the test never checks that an update keeps the same store.

Save the id from the first call and compare the updated store's id against it.

held.title: Store create may be a bulk endpoint returning an array
held.body:
Cloudflare's `POST /secrets_store/stores` appears to take an array body (`[{name}]`) and return `result` as an array.

If so, the plain object body is rejected, or `result.id` is undefined and an empty id is stored in state. Every later call then targets `/stores/undefined`.

I could not check the current API shape. Verify it, and read `result[0].id` if the endpoint is bulk.

held.title: Bulk secret delete sends names where the API likely expects secret ids
held.body:
`listSecrets` throws away the secret ids and returns only names. `deleteSecrets` then sends an array of names to `DELETE .../secrets`.

Cloudflare's bulk delete identifies secrets by id. The removal of stale secrets on update will likely fail or do nothing, leaving removed secrets in the store.

I could not confirm the exact API contract from here. Keep the ids from the list call and send those instead.
